speaker: Head Coach
quote_text:
Congratulations, Ange. You must be delighted  with the maturity of your team tonight.  
Yeah, I'm delighted with many things and  yeah, super proud of the lads. Look, yeah,  
you're playing away from home, quarter-final,  and it's a very good side. You know,  
you're going to have to work really hard,  be well organised and disciplined, and also,  
you know, we needed to score tonight, so we needed  to show the quality we have as well. And to a man,  
I just thought they were outstanding. Yeah, so  proud of them, you know, in such a big game,  
they delivered a performance that, you know, means  we're through to the semi-final. And, you know,  
I think over the two legs, I think we deserve to  go through, you know, so I could well have been  
over in the first leg, but again, we've earned the  right to be in the semi. Gary. Congratulations.  
After a difficult season with injuries, etc, do  you kind of have a sixth sense that Tottenham's  
name might be on this trophy? No, I don't, I don't  think that way, but yeah, from our perspective,  
look, yeah, it's we've had a difficult season.  I think there's some reasoning behind that, that  
you know, which is pretty evident tonight that you  know, when we've got our strongest team out there,  
a lot of the things that we've sort of suffered  with this year, I'm sure we wouldn't have, because  
you know, the spine of our team, the you know,  at times, Vicario, Romero, van de Ven, Bentancur,  
Solanke, like these guys, we were missing all of  them at different times this year. And, you know,  
we've got the whole group, and it's not just them,  it's the whole group together. You know, we know  
that we can be a team that's pretty compelling  against anybody. And, you know, we're in the  
Final Four now, so we give ourselves a chance.  Jay. Hi Ange, congratulations. I saw you walked  
down the tunnel at the end of the game with your  arm around James Maddison. Just wanted to check  
in on how he's doing after what happened. Yeah,  he's fine. Unbelievable courage in that moment,  
you know, to put his body on the line, knowing  full well he was going to, you know, got my pretty  
severe knock. I mean, I was surprised it wasn't  a red card, but yeah, super courageous from him.  
And look, he's sore, but I'm sure that's all been  knowing that, you know, he's helped us progress  
through a semi. Matt. Hello, Ange. I was going to  ask you about that as well. Are you warming to VAR  
tonight? Are you pleased with the intervention  or are you still a bit crossed that it wasn't a  
red card? No, well, you know, I mean, we can be  a bit sort of facetious about that, Matt, but I  
thought it was a clear penalty. I'm not sure why  it needed VAR. I mean, when a player wins the ball  
and it gets cleaned up, if that was a defender, it  would definitely be probably a red card now it's a  
goalkeeper, so maybe it's definitely a penalty.  I don't think that needed a review. So, again,  
I think we got what we deserved. George. Hi,  Ange. Congratulations. You've always had belief  
in this squad and this team, but I'm guessing you  probably couldn't say really strongly, you know,  
to everyone, you're going to win the Europa League  before this two tyres. How much confidence do  
you have in this squad now to go all the way  and deliver what the fans have wanted for so  
long? Well, look, I mean, I think, you know, we  can't get too far ahead of ourselves. You know,  
in the semi-final, you know, we're going to have  a difficult opponent in the semi, but it's not  
about my belief in the team. I think what's more  important is the belief the team's had, you know,  
because after a season like ours, it would be very  easy for the players and the staff to, you know,  
I've said before, you know, that they could have  left me in a pretty vulnerable place in terms of,  
you know, them splintering at any, but I've never  felt that, you know, with all the noise around,  
you know, our season, you know, they've been  so united in believing in what we're trying  
to achieve here. And that's what gave me hard  all along that, you know, if we've got our own  
little bit of slice of luck in terms of just  getting some players back, that you know,  
I really believe that this team, you know, could  achieve and that's what, you know, keeps driving  
me. It's not so much my belief in them, it's  their belief in, in what we're doing and both,  
you know, and the players and staff have just been  outstanding. Like I said, you know, I'm, you know,  
I'm the front, I'm the front man for it, but, you  know, they take responsibility for it as well for  
all my decisions and everything I do, but not  at any stage have I felt that they've lost any  
belief in me or what we're doing. And that's just  crucial when you're having a difficult season,  
but there's also a season of opportunity there.  Ryan to finish, please. Hi Ange, congratulations.  
I just wanted to ask about your own kind of  personal feelings. Obviously it's no secret,  
it's been a tough season and coming into this game  it must have been quite tough having to deal with  
all the noise. So to win in the manner in which  you did, how are you kind of feeling as a relief?  
I think I said yesterday. I'm the same manager  today that I was yesterday. So people think that  
us winning tonight makes me a better manager.  Whoever didn't think I was doing a good job  
yesterday should be feeling the same way today.  I don't care. It doesn't bother me. It doesn't  
affect what I do. For me, it's always about the  dressing room, you know. Do the players believe,  
do the staff believe? That's much more  important than what others may, you know,  
make of me. So unfortunately for a lot of  you, you're going to have to put up with me  
for a little bit longer, mate. So we'll just see  how that goes. All right. Thank you very much.
title: Ange Postecoglou post-match press conference | Eintracht Frankfurt 0-1 Tottenham Hotspur (Agg 1-2)
